searchText: yeah something does seem off, i'll have to pull down some prater data to see what is going on My prysm node reports that 50 and 51 are not canonical so that would explain it And the point is that 53 is based on 49 So it's the right behavior to finalize 49 as state cc <@!881905303011086387> also cc <@!97774605351010304> <@!471975503859810316> This block and its parent should appear as "orphaned" in the explorer <https://prater.beaconcha.in/block/1183551> Which also raises the question why Lodestar decided to skip 2 valid blocks, it doesn't seem to be timing cause they where up to 36 seconds earlier, Nimbus then built on Loderstar's block, and I think they shouldn't have either: surely weight was higher to build on top of 51 than 53 isn't it? yeah that would explain it and it does suggest some kind of explorer bug could be a slow fork choice / processing? Yeah I don't know about the explorer, what slightly worries me is Lodestar + Nimbus behavior here, leaving a fork with three slots and two blocks in them not accounted for is weird. And Nimbus had no reason to vote for Lodestar's block unless it also didn't see the fork at all. Look at Lodestar's block: understandably it had only 300 votes <https://prater.beaconcha.in/block/1183553> which is what I would expect on a bad block. Nimbus' next block had no reason to build on it, am I wrong? when nimbus proposes that block, there's already 4 blocks in the fork, plenty of time to see those votes. Nimbus' block is also not highly voted Which slot was Altair's fork for Prater? this may have been a change of Sync committee: there's zero participation in those two first blocks. Nope, it's not
